1. GENERAL INFORMATION

1.1 Purpose. This attachment provides the estimated workload data for PWS Part 5, Food Services, and PWS Part 6, Facility Sanitation (Custodial) Services. The workload data is the Government’s best estimate of the requirement and is provided for proposal preparation; it is not a guarantee of the volume of work to be ordered or performed. Workload data was compiled by the Installation Food Program Manager (IFPM), Logistics Readiness Center (LRC) Fort Branford, from the Army Food Management Information System (AFMIS) and the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) real property inventory.

1.2 Scope Summary. The Contractor shall provide all management, supervision, labor and non-Government-furnished supplies necessary to perform the following services at Fort Branford, Georgia, in accordance with Army Regulation (AR) 30-22, The Army Food Program, and Department of the Army Pamphlet (DA PAM) 30-22, Operating Procedures for the Army Food Program:

  1. Full Food Service (FFS) at two (2) Warrior Restaurants (dining facilities), Buildings 4120 and 7031: receipt and storage of subsistence, food preparation, cooking, serving, headcount and cashier operations, dining facility sanitation (kitchen, serving lines, dish room, pot and pan room and dining rooms), and remote site feeding when ordered.
  2. Dining Facility Attendant (DFA) services at one (1) Warrior Restaurant, Building 9215. Building 9215 supports Table of Organization and Equipment (TOE) units; in accordance with AR 30-22, dining facility operations in support of TOE organizations are authorized to contract for DFA services only. Cooking and food production at Building 9215 are performed by Government (military) 92G Culinary Specialists. The Contractor provides DFA services: dining room and serving line sanitation, dish and tray washing, pot and pan washing, bussing tables, restocking beverage, salad and condiment stations, trash removal, and headcount/cashier duties.
  3. Facility sanitation (custodial) services for the facilities listed in TE 6-1, at the frequencies shown. Custodial services for these facilities were moved from the former DPW custodial contract into this requirement at award of the current contract (paragraph 1.4).

Subsistence for all dining facilities is Government-furnished through the Troop Issue Subsistence Activity (TISA). Dining facilities, equipment and expendable supplies are furnished as listed in TE 3.

1.3 Period of Performance. The period of performance consists of one (1) twelve-month base period (1 April 2027 – 31 March 2028) and four (4) twelve-month option periods, plus a potential extension of services of up to six (6) months under FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services.

1.4 Current Contract (For Information Only). The services described in PWS Parts 5 and 6 are currently performed by Sandhill Garrison Services, LLC under Contract No. W9124J-21-C-0012, a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract awarded on 24 September 2021. The contract consists of a twelve-month base period (1 October 2021 – 30 September 2022) and four twelve-month option periods, with a total contract value, inclusive of all option periods, of $71,284,960. The annual value of the current option period (Option Period 4, 1 October 2025 – 30 September 2026) is $14,962,415. An extension of services under FAR 52.217-8 was exercised for the period 1 October 2026 through 31 March 2027 in the amount of $7,481,208. At the time of the current award, the requirement included four (4) dining facilities; Building 2240 has been closed since 1 November 2024 (see TE 5-1, Note 4). These values are as modified: Modification P00009 deleted the Building 2240 line items effective 1 November 2024 and increased the Building 4120 line items for the reassigned diners, so the Option Period 4 value covers three (3) operating dining facilities (4120, 7031 and 9215) and the TE 6-1 custodial facilities, plus Building 1475 through 30 June 2026. Field feeding and remote site support for unit training exercises is ordered separately under Contract No. W9124J-24-D-0019 (ceiling $4,950,000) and is not part of this requirement.

1.5 Basis of the Estimated Workload. TE 5-1 states the estimated average headcount for each meal period for a typical week of operation: five (5) weekdays (Monday through Friday) and two (2) weekend days (Saturday and Sunday). Training holidays and Federal holidays are served on the weekend and holiday schedule (brunch and supper) shown in TE 5-2. The averages are computed from AFMIS headcount data for the twelve months ending 30 June 2026 and have been adjusted by the IFPM for unit stationing projected for FY27 (increases of about 1% to 2%). Building 2240 was closed for that entire period; its diners were reassigned to Building 4120 on 1 November 2024 and are already included in the Building 4120 averages. Offerors shall base their staffing and pricing on the average headcounts in TE 5-1 applied to fifty-two (52) typical weeks per year. Weekday training and Federal holidays shall not be priced as additional weekend days. The historical meals served in TE 5-3 are provided for information only; the FY 2024 and October 2024 figures include Building 2240 operations and Building 4120 before consolidation.

1.6 Headcount. “Headcount” is the number of diners served during a meal period, all diner categories combined: Soldiers subsisting in kind (meal card holders), Soldiers receiving Basic Allowance for Subsistence and Department of Defense civilians paying cash or using the DD Form 1544 (Cash Meal Payment Sheet), and authorized guests. The Contractor shall record headcount for each meal period using the AFMIS point-of-sale system and Common Access Card (CAC) scanners and shall provide headcount data to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) weekly. At Building 9215 (DFA), the Contractor performs headcount and cashier duties under the supervision of the Government Dining Facility Manager.

1.7 Maximum Feeding Capacity. The maximum feeding capacity for a meal period is the seating capacity of the dining facility multiplied by three (3) seat turns. Feeding at maximum capacity is required infrequently (for example, unit deployment and redeployment, organization days and holiday meals) and is stated in TE 5-1 for planning of storage, workforce and equipment only. Maximum feeding capacity is not the estimated workload.

1.8 Changes in Workload. Increases or decreases in the average daily headcount of more than fifteen percent (15%) sustained for sixty (60) consecutive days, the opening or closure of a dining facility, or the addition or deletion of a facility in TE 6-1 shall be addressed by contract modification. Building 2240 (Dragon Warrior Restaurant) is projected to reopen after completion of renovation in FY28 and may be added by bilateral modification during an option period.

NOTES:

1/ Average headcount is the average number of diners served per meal period (all diner categories, see paragraph 1.6). Monday – Friday averages apply to five (5) weekdays per week; Weekends & Holidays averages apply to Saturdays and Sundays (two (2) days in a typical week), and the same brunch/supper schedule is served on training and Federal holidays. Headcounts are per meal period, not per day. Price fifty-two (52) typical weeks per year (paragraph 1.5).

2/ Seating capacity is the number of seats in the dining room(s), including outdoor seating where provided.

3/ Maximum feeding capacity per meal period = seating capacity × 3 seat turns (paragraph 1.7). For planning of storage, workforce and equipment only; it is not the estimated workload.

4/ Building 2240 (Dragon Warrior Restaurant) is closed for renovation (SRM project 2240-24-R) from 1 November 2024 through the end of FY27 (30 September 2027). 5/ Late/Midnight meal (2330–0100) is served Monday through Friday at Building 7031 only. No midnight meal is served on weekends or holidays.

6/ At Building 9215 the Contractor provides DFA services only (PWS paragraph 5.3). Food production, menu planning and subsistence accountability are performed by the Government Dining Facility Manager and military cooks.

7/ Totals are provided for information. Totals are the sum of meal-period averages across dining facilities and are not a daily headcount.

Brunch and supper. On weekends and holidays the breakfast and lunch meal periods are combined into a single brunch meal period and the dinner meal period is served as supper. Hours of operation for each meal period are in TE 5-2.

TECHNICAL EXHIBIT 6-1 (CONTINUED)
NOTES TO THE FACILITY LIST

1/ Custodial Service Area is the portion of the gross area that receives custodial service under PWS Part 6. Mechanical rooms, electrical and communications closets, warehouse and storage bays, and areas cleaned by others are excluded.

2/ Dining facilities (Buildings 4120, 7031 and 9215): kitchen, serving line, dish room, pot and pan room, and dining room sanitation is performed under PWS Part 5 (FFS at Buildings 4120 and 7031; DFA at Building 9215) and is not included in the Custodial Service Area. Custodial service under PWS Part 6 covers restrooms, entries, corridors and administrative offices. Each dining facility appears once in TE 5-1 (food service workload) and once in this exhibit (custodial workload); they are the same buildings.

3/ Frequency codes: 7X/WK – seven days per week, including holidays; 5X/WK – Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays; 3X/WK – Monday, Wednesday and Friday; 2X/WK – two non-consecutive days per week as scheduled with the building manager; 1X/WK – once per week. Task frequencies for each code are in TE 6-2 (Attachment J-0505).

4/ Building 1475 was deleted from the facility list by the DPW real property office on 30 June 2026 and will not be serviced. It is shown for reconciliation with the current contract only.

5/ The total includes only the sixteen (16) facilities in scope. Building 1475 (deleted) and Building 2240 (closed) are not included in the total.

6-1.1 Facilities Not Included

The following facilities are serviced under other contracts or by the occupant and are not included in this requirement: Buildings 5100 and 5104 (Branford Army Health Clinic; Medical Readiness Command custodial contract); Building 4810 (Outdoor Pool; seasonal, MWR); Unaccompanied Housing Buildings 8101 through 8104 (residential communities initiative); and the Exchange Main Store and food court (Army and Air Force Exchange Service).

6-1.2 Building Access

Building managers will provide keys and access rosters. Custodial service at 5X/WK facilities shall be performed between 1700 and 0600 unless otherwise approved by the COR. Custodial service at dining facilities shall not be performed during meal periods shown in TE 5-2.

Prepared by: Installation Food Program Manager, Logistics Readiness Center Fort Branford, and DPW Real Property Office. Point of contact for questions: Contracting Officer, MICC – Fort Sam Houston. Questions shall be submitted in writing in accordance with Section L.
